description: Intent i019 (SNAPSHOT=s02, BRANCH=terminator-write-off-by-one) concluded with an evidence-backed bounded NEGATIVE result: no NEW clamp-then-terminate off-by-one terminator site exists in snapshots/s02 beyond the already-known pair. The final artifact is at /mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C10/agent-state/findings/i019.json (findings: [], candidates: 18, execution_status: complete, snapshots_checked: ["s02"]). Search evidence: enumerated 340 tree-wide terminator writes of the form buf[idx]=0/'\0' at user-derived indices (len/count/size/cnt/n/length families) in s02; filtered to 121 with a usercopy primitive (copy_from_user/memdup_user/simple_write_to_buffer) within 30 preceding lines; each triaged by function-context bound analysis against declarations, guards, and clamps. Every site enforces one of the safe primitives: (a) 'count >= sizeof(buf)' rejection before copy (fnic 152/509, snic 120, mt7915 68/1073/1337, mt7996 70/912, mac80211 133/189/280/397, trace 5361/7096, trace_hwlat 694, trace_osnoise 2223, user_namespace 1234 kbuf[8], netdevsim 259, i40e 1700, ixgbe 83/166, vgaarb 1175, test_udelay 112, sched/debug 138/182/233, iommu 697 cnt>63, viafbdev 1470 count>63, hisilicon qm/hpre/sec2/zip, habanalabs, adf_heartbeat 172 count!=2, acpi/proc 103, rtas-proc 269, lpar 514/611, via-pmu 933, intel/pmc 930, i915 1040/1121/304, drm_debugfs 419, armada 69, lsdc 647, smackfs 6 sites, binfmt_elf len>=ELF_PRARGSZ, lkdtm 247/324 + srm_env 107 count>=PAGE_SIZE, scsi_devinfo 732 length<PAGE_SIZE branch, sunrpc cache 1521 + svcauth_gss 1420 count>sizeof(tbuf)-1); (b) a sizeof(...)-1 clamp (yurex 460, pkeys 152, tlb 1327, picolcd 48, wiimote 141, iio 415, chipidea 88, toshiba 1490/1671/1742, ath5k/ath6kl/ath9k/ath10k/ath11k spectral+debug, libipw 233, cxgb4 674/1294, dma/debug 760, kstrtox 403/417, configfs fill_write_buffer 195, libfs 1319, spufs 125); (c) a +1-sized allocation (apparmorfs aa_simple_write_to_buffer(size+1) then data->data[size]=0; i40e:776 kzalloc(count+1); rvu_debugfs:1006 memdup_user(count+1); wil6210 kmalloc(len+1); rbd 6249/6502 kmemdup(len+1)); or (d) no terminator write at all (kernel/power/qos.c:388 and kernel/profile.c:440 count==sizeof(s32) acceptances are fixed-size binary copies with no terminator; pktgen buf[len]=0 is bounded by strn_len(..., sizeof(...)-1); hfi1 fault.c:194 is a read-side formatter inside kcalloc(1280)). The scsi host ->write_info PAGE_SIZE boundary case named by the intent is safe in s02: scsi_proc.c:42/71 PROC_BLOCK_SIZE = 3*1024 = 3072 < PAGE_SIZE, so wd33c93_write_info's buf[len]='\0' (wd33c93.c:2021, len<=3072) is in-bounds inside the 4096-byte page, and imm.c:132/ppa.c:132 write no terminator. The two already-reported instances were cited as known, not re-reported: drivers/edac/versal_edac.c:863 (inject_data_ue_store, char buf[6], len=min_t(size_t,count,sizeof(buf)) without -1, buf[6]=0 when count>=6) and drivers/edac/zynqmp_edac.c:311 (inject_ue_write, same pattern), both ASan-verified by intent i007/f015. Limitations: the sweep used a 30-line usercopy-proximity window and specific index spellings, so a terminator write farther from its copy, inside a helper, or at an unusual index could evade it; the ath5k debugfs family (lines 234/336/441/614/763/861) is left unresolved because each handler prints the safe -1 clamp but also an 'if (len > sizeof(buf))' guard form that was not traced to its consuming index before finalization (likely safe); bulk families (ath/mediatek/mac80211/toshiba/smackfs etc.) were classified from their printed guard/clamp lines, not deep-read function bodies; ioctl/compat_ioctl/io_uring/module_param surfaces were covered only through the shared grep families; no in-kernel KASAN run was performed (read-only snapshot) - all classifications rest on line-level bound analysis.
